sink.buffer: Renderer buffer 0.5–4 sec, variable session-to-session, NOT exposed via UPnP. AVTransport::GetPositionInfo reports the queue position, not the DAC position; the hidden buffer between them shifts ±600ms across sessions on the same hardware.

transport.metadataNote: Empty metadata required. Sending DIDL-Lite metadata returns UPnP error 714.

quirks: x-rincon-mp3radio:// URI scheme tells Sonos to treat the stream as continuous internet radio (no seekable track). Required for live capture; using a generic http:// URI puts the Playbar in 'fetching media metadata' mode that takes 30+ sec to resolve.

Pump-before-SOAP ordering required. Sonos's SetAVTransportURI handler opens the HTTP URL during the SOAP call and expects audio bytes within ~5 sec. Start the audio pump BEFORE issuing SetAVTransportURI or both sides time out (chicken-and-egg).

Sonos playback timing is encrypted at the wire level — there's NO public API to shift Sonos playback forward/backward. The Sonos Android app's 75–2000ms 'line-in delay' slider uses encrypted UPnP traffic that the most thorough public reverse-engineering project (svrooij/node-sonos-ts) explicitly gave up on. See node-sonos-ts#139.

GetPositionInfo.RelTime is unreliable for sync math. It reports the renderer queue position, not the DAC position. The hidden buffer between them varies ~600ms session-to-session on the same hardware. Mic-based calibration (chirp + cross-correlation) bypasses this entirely — measures actual sound at the listening position.

Inter-session variance: Sonos's effective playback lag varies session-to-session even on the same hardware. A calibration that worked perfectly in one Play All can be off by 600ms in the next. Per-session re-calibration via mic chirp is the only reliable cross-protocol sync mechanism.

control.fallbackStrategy: Poll RenderingControl::GetVolume on demand; Sonos doesn't have a 'powered off' state via UPnP (it's always-on standby until commanded).

notes: Original Playbar without AirPlay 2 support. Lives behind the 'older Sonos hardware that the modern ecosystem forgot' use case — exactly the kind of device SuperAudio exists for. M4 audible-test passing device. Documented inter-session buffer variance is the reason the chirp-based mic calibration matters for cross-protocol sync.
